Having put WAY too many hours into this game (somewhere around 1200), I can safely say this is a very good game. It's not quite up to Persona 4 Golden levels of good, but it's damn good. The story is enjoyable, the cast of characters is humorous, and a little more up to date that P4G. It is also a delight to see Igor return again. Royals content is hands down the best part of this game. Again, not quite the best out of any persona game, but I have a hard time saying that.

This game, in general, is a pretty damn good game. I would LOVE to recommend it. But I cannot do so in good faith, when the game locks a huge amount of content behind an invisible and arbitrary condition. An entire third semester is unavailable if you don't fully level your relationship with a particular side character. If you're the type to go into a game blind and experience it fresh, theres a good chance you'll just miss out, with no way of knowing what to do to get the extra content. Play it if you want, but google "how to get the third semester no spoilers p5r" or something like that before playing.

This was the first time I finished a Persona game and I personally think it's one of the best ones. The "Royal" version of Persona 5 comes with all DLCs included plus an extended storyline and easily nets 50-80 hours.
However, there are some things that may be annoying for completionists here I'd like to point out later on.

Positive:
- Good story with some twists
- Many cool Personas with different skills to collect and use
- Interesting side stories (and there are A LOT)
- Very unique Soundtrack
- Stylish visuals and effects that stay true to the Persona series
- Lots of things to do, plenty of content
- Funny tropes and humor
- All the DLC for free

Neutral:
- I wish you could give skill cards to your party members Personas
- Achieving the True Ending in one playthrough is very hard, especially on a blind playthrough. There is New Game+ to make it trivial on the second run, but I'd rather the requirements for the True Ending weren't so high, so someone who doesn't like to play through a game more than once could get the fulfillment in one go.
- The True Ending is required to get all achievements.

Negative:
- Mementos is way too long, boring and repetitive for it's position in the plot.

This game is very meaningful

In the prologue, the game states that the story is purely fictional and has no relevance to reality. But what I want to say is that the dark and cruel social problems are in reality.

Public officials abuse their power, celebrities steal wealth, underground forces collude with officials and businessmen, and unscrupulous companies exploit their employees. All of these are inseparable from the support of the government

The game describes a country that has twisted and turned to dictatorship, where politicians manipulate people's hearts and monopolize power，Oppressed young people rise up in rebellion

I have been a fan of Persona series since P3:FES, but I don't have console anymore. So when P5R came to PC, it is a must buy for me.

What I like the most from Persona series is their Social Link System. In addition to the traditional JRPG gameplay like tactical battle, dungeon crawling, you need to socializing with your friends and people around Tokyo (in P5). This social event not only give you side story, it also give you benefit (skills, buff, etc) next time you explore the dungeon again.

In terms of gameplay, graphic and quality of life, P5R is absolutely upgraded from P3 and P4. The story is good, it have corruption, mental health and related to our society right now.

If you never play persona series, I think P5R is good entry point for the series.

Kawakami & Haru supremacy

Persona 5 Royal is an exceptional JRPG that masterfully blends style, substance, and storytelling into an unforgettable experience. From the moment you step into its striking red-and-black aesthetic, the game oozes confidence and personality. Its slick user interface, jazzy soundtrack, and fluid animations make even simple menu navigation feel exciting and polished.

The story is one of the game’s strongest elements, tackling mature themes like corruption, identity, and rebellion while still delivering heartfelt character moments. The Phantom Thieves are a memorable cast, each with meaningful personal arcs that make their growth feel earned and emotionally satisfying. Royal enhances the original narrative with new characters and an expanded third semester, adding depth and a powerful emotional payoff that elevates the entire story.

Gameplay is equally impressive. The turn-based combat is fast, strategic, and highly rewarding, with refinements in Royal that make battles smoother and more engaging than ever. Life-simulation elements—such as managing time, building relationships, and improving skills—create a perfect balance between dungeon crawling and everyday life, making each in-game day feel valuable.

Overall, Persona 5 Royal is a definitive RPG experience and one of the finest games of its generation. Whether you’re a longtime fan or a newcomer to the series, it offers hundreds of hours of stylish, emotionally rich, and deeply satisfying gameplay that’s hard to put down. 🎭✨

Good RPG but I mean, no news here seeing as the game has plenty of reviews all over the internet. However, everyone has their own tastes and preferences. So for me, it actually took me a while to really start feeling it and get into it. It is definitely way over-hyped imo; it has plenty flaws, both in writing, down to gameplay mechanics and lack of player agency a lot of the time. I got it back when it first released on the Playstation and lost interest around 3rd palace, it wasn't awful but also didn't really grab me enough to choose to play it more over other things I could be doing. 

Now, years later, I decided to give it another shot seeing it on sale on Steam. Having fully played through it this time I can say it's, despite its flaws, a really solid game. And a loooong game. But, I actually didn't feel it was too long, go figure. Yeah, after about 30 hours or so of kind of thinking the game was just okay; not bad nor amazing, I got really pulled in and hooked and wound up playing it for hours on end on my days off. I think the plot getting thicker and more characters I actually enjoyed joining helped a lot. So, all in all, as a whole, I do think the game is pretty good and worth playing through. I am glad I finally did so in the end.

that being said, the third semester added in royal is leagues better than the base game in terms of writing. i find the ending of the base game to be super lackluster and honestly, it still stings as an overall low point for the game.

would recommend, even to people who aren't a fan of the genre.

I haven't enjoyed a JRPG in a long time. I find they like to waste a lot of my time with slow, boring combat. The "roleplaying" is usually next to nothing, where none of the player decisions affect the gameplay or story. The stories are predictable or total eye-rolling nonsense anyway, so I almost never notice. The "anime" aesthetic is overdone and boring, and if I have to listen to one more garbage orchestral soundtrack while I watch predictable, melodramatic dialogue, I'm just gonna lose it.

But because this game fixes every single one of those problems, this is one of the best games I've ever played. And that's coming from someone who didn't even bother to finish Persona 3 FES or 4 Golden. It took me over a hundred hours to beat on PS4, and it was worth going in on again here. Even if it doesn't sound like your kind of thing, give it a shot. The day-to-day life sim stuff works crazy well when it comes to working with other parts of the game, and it's worth going back to for the vibes alone.

There's so much to say about P5R, and in those cases, I prefer to keep it short, because no one wants to read a review that takes up a whole page.

If you haven't played P5 before, it's an excellent JRPG/VN mashup with a great plot, fun turn-based combat, and interesting characters, that can entertain even the biggest RPG hater (I personally am not a huge fan of the genre). If you've played the vanilla P5 game, they've improved everything, fixed the bigger issues the game had, and added amazing new content both before and after the postgame. It's one of the biggest no-brainers I've ever seen, even at full price. However, that's pretty expensive, and it has already gone on sale a couple of times, so waiting for a drop shouldn't be too hard.

Basically, do you like JRPGs? If so, buy this game. If you don't, I still think it's worth a shot, so pick it up on sale or something. Easy 10/10.

Imagine still thinking P3 or P4G are better in 2026. Absolute nostalgia-blinded cope. Persona 5 Royal is objectively the pinnacle of the JRPG genre. Every other game’s UI looks like a 1990s Excel spreadsheet compared to this masterpiece. The soundtrack has no business being this fire, and the style is just untouchable. And don’t even get me started on the third semester—Maruki is the best-written antagonist in gaming history, period. If you haven't played this yet, you're not just missing a game; you're missing a cultural reset. Stop playing "mid" games and join the Phantom Thieves. If you think it’s "too long," you just lack the attention span for a 10/10 experience. The GOAT. No competition. 🎭🔥

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (96%): players love the story and characters, which 59% of reviews praise, and they also praise the gameplay and combat.
The most common complaints are that the combat feels shallow and the story predictable.

details.text: Story complaints have eased lately, with 5% of recent reviews complaining about the story and characters, well below the all-time share.
Players who have just started are less positive, at 88%, than players with the most hours, at 97%.
